title: Handle optional upload query parameters without mutating callers
body:
### Motivation and context

Closes #11481.

Uploader.upload_file accepts omitted query parameters, but the final request assigns its server-provided filename into None after the TUS transfer has completed. Passing a mapping avoids the exception but mutates the caller's mapping, so reusing it can send a stale filename in a later upload-start request.

Create a private dictionary before starting the existing upload sequence. Keep its supplied values and add the final filename to that private copy.

### How has this been tested?

- Exact final commit: `43956cb1aa0233ae579028c310944c6246ccde5b`.
- Native generated SDK and real HTTP transport against a local protocol peer.
- Final validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/cvat/actions/runs/43310465808
- All 13 new cases pass; all 13 fail against the original implementation.
- 48 existing mask/attribute unit cases pass.
- Black and isort checks pass.

The tests cover omitted, explicit None, empty, and populated parameters; zero-byte, small, and multi-chunk files; actual upload-start/finish requests and complete transferred bytes; and reuse of one mapping for two files. They assert that the original mapping is unchanged.

### Scope and risks

The test peer implements the HTTP upload protocol exercised by the native client; this is not a full CVAT service integration test. Retry policy, chunk sizing, filename validation, and supplied query values are unchanged.

### Checklist

- [x] Based on `develop`.
- [x] Added a changelog fragment and regression tests.
- [x] Preserved the existing transfer protocol and caller-supplied values.
- [x] Documentation impact: existing optional parameter contract is restored.
